resolution:
Both root-caused and fixed.

ee09_merge_variables_test.zig TC-ISS-202-01: the raw PgError.ServerError chain was two compounding bugs, each revealed after fixing the prior one -- (1) the hand-rolled INSERT INTO instance_definition_snapshots omitted the NOT NULL definition_name/definition_ver columns; (2) after fixing that, a second hand-rolled INSERT INTO tasks failed on tasks.token_id's NOT NULL FK into tokens, which this raw-SQL setup never populated at all. Rather than patch each missing column one at a time, replaced the entire hand-rolled raw-SQL instance/task setup (instance_projections + instance_definition_snapshots + tasks INSERTs) with the same activate()+create()+list() pattern every other sibling test in this file already uses correctly (def_store.activate, inst_store.create, task_store.list) -- this routes through the real engine, which populates every required column/FK correctly. Also fixed a genuine, separate isolation bug found in the same test: its process_definitions cleanup defer was registered at the very END of the test function (170+ lines after definition creation), so any earlier try-failure exited the function before the defer was ever registered, permanently orphaning a DuplicateNameVersion-colliding row for every subsequent run. Moved the defer to immediately after definition creation, matching every sibling test's pattern. Manually cleaned the one pre-existing orphaned row left by an earlier failed run. Verified: zig build test-integration-ee09 -- 5/5 pass, re-run twice to confirm the cleanup fix prevents recurrence.

effects_subsystem_test.zig TC-EXP-301-09: root cause was NOT a stale test expectation or adapter-stub drift as originally hypothesized -- it was a genuine pool-exhaustion bug in src/effects/worker.zig's sweepOnce(), the same nested-pool.acquire()-under-a-held-lease class as GH-521/ISS-0187. sweepOnce() acquired its own connection and held it (via defer) for its ENTIRE body, including the loop that calls processRow() -- which itself acquires additional connections per row for delivery-result updates, retry/DLQ marking, and engine re-entry. Under EffectsPoolFixture's pool_size=2 test harness (one connection already held by the test's own h.conn), sweepOnce's own held connection left ZERO free connections for processRow's nested acquire(), which failed and was silently swallowed by `catch return` -- so email delivery succeeded internally but the outbox row's status update never landed, leaving it permanently 'pending'. Fixed by releasing sweepOnce's fetch connection before entering the row-processing loop, since it is only needed for the initial fetchDueRows query. Verified: zig build test-integration-effects-subsystem -- 32/32 pass (was 31/32).

Incidental finding filed separately (not fixed here): ISS-0650/GH-657 -- TC-EXP-301-08 (a sibling test, unrelated to either fix above) leaks 3 allocations on the duplicate-idempotency-key code path in event_store store.append/rowToEventRecord. Does not fail the test (passes 32/32); a DebugAllocator diagnostic only.
